title: Recurring unresolved limitation 'ecological-validity' across 3 independent papers
explanation: 3 independent papers (2012–2026) report an own-work limitation normalized to 'ecological-validity'. Mixed-fidelity: 3 full-text, 0 abstract-only; score corrected for the ~11x full-text detection bias = 0.650 vs uncorrected 0.650. Methodological diversity: 7 distinct methods (NOTE: diversity/time-span weighting extends beyond opportunity-criteria.md). Resolution is ASSUMED absent — no limitation-resolution relation exists in Phase 3, so 'unresolved' is unverified. evidence_trail.text: Healthy snacks at the checkout counter: A lab and field study on the impact of shelf arrangement and assortment structure on consumer choices
Consumer effects of front-of-package nutrition labeling: an interdisciplinary meta-analysis
An accuracy self-nudge to reduce misinformation sharing online.
All included primary studies assume consumer awareness of the label, whereas attention and motivation at point-of-purchase vary in real retail environments.
The choice task in the lab study had an artificial nature and relied exclusively on student participants.

In the captive nudge condition, participants were forced to respond to the prompt rather than being permitted to ignore or opt out as in real-world deployments, conferring an artificial advantage to the captive nudge.

consumer.headline: 3 separate teams ran into the same wall: ecological validity
consumer.kind_short: A problem that several independent teams ran into
consumer.kind_long: Papers describe the limits of their own work. When separate teams — who did not build on each other — keep reporting the same limit, that is a sign of a real obstacle rather than one group's bad luck.
consumer.strength_meaning: There is real evidence behind this, but it rests on a small number of papers — read them before trusting it.
consumer.why: 3 separate research teams each reported hitting this in their own work. They did not build on each other, so this is unlikely to be one group's bad luck. Their papers span 1 year. We could read 3 of them in full, which is where teams describe what actually went wrong.

caveats.label: Only counted within these 45 papers
caveats.text: These teams all hit this problem within this library of 45 papers, not the whole field. Work outside it may already have solved it. Check before you invest.
